title: Chapter 1864: Liyuan Theater (II)
content:
Chapter 1864: Liyuan Theater (II)

Night lay deep around the hushed courtyard. A plaintive melody rose and fell in long phrases, its lingering notes curling about the rafters.

"A household drowned in blood, a year steeped in hate... I beat upon my forebears' doors; why does no reply come? Have all the stars and moon come to naught... The loyal perish, the treacherous survive. Trace cause and consequence once more, and dark waters swallow the prison gate!"

People stood shoulder to shoulder inside the Liyuan Theater, watching the stage in silence. Outside the courtyard, firelight flickered beneath a pot of simmering medicine. Beside it sat an old man whose hair and beard were silver, though his frame remained sturdy, gently working a fan. When the time came, he added medicinal pills, poured the medicine out in three portions, and let it cool before carrying it upstairs.

"How laughable! How laughable! Before the ancestral stele, before the ancestral stele... the land lies shrouded in the smoke of war. I have crossed every mountain, every ridge, yet gained only sleepless nights..."

The dharma lamps upstairs shone more dimly, and there were few spectators. A single table stood beside the railing, with someone leaning over it, while a young master stood nearby. Several theatrical robes hung on the wall, their dark red sleeves stirring gently in the breeze.

Holding the tray, the old man called, "Old ancestor..."

Only then did the man at the table turn his gaze away from the stage below. His hair and beard were entirely white, and he looked somewhat withered. "Shuya... Set it down for now."

"Yes."

Li Xuanxuan looked at him with clouded old eyes and said, "Leave these things to the servants... You are getting old yourself. Do not wear yourself out."

Li Shuya was Li Quewan's elder brother. After some trouble years ago, he had been sent to attend Li Xuanxuan. Decades had passed in the blink of an eye. The young man had become old, yet remained as meticulous as ever.

No one knew the elder's failing health more directly than Li Shuya. He glanced at the cup and stood silently to one side, waiting.

Li Xuanxuan could only pick up the cup and quickly drink its contents. Setting down his manuscript, he said, "However good the pills, there is a limit to what they can do. They offer little benefit now. Tell Jiangzong that there's no need to send any more here."

"Yes."

Li Shuya silently carried the cup outside. Before long, beneath the lingering strains of song, came the clinking of the porcelain stove as he stubbornly resumed brewing medicine. Li Xuanxuan could only sigh, his gaze settling quietly on the theatrical costume hanging in the room.

The costume was crimson throughout, embroidered with gleaming gold and paired with a colorful crown. In the Liyuan Theater, an actor wearing it usually portrayed a ruler of the Li Family, sometimes carrying a bow on his back and a sword at his waist. Recent examples included [A Tale of Usurpation], the tragedy of the Jiang and Yu Families, and [Driving Out the Villains], which recounted the Li Family's rise.

After all, Jiangzong, Jiangqian, and Jianglong have all worn the same family head's attire in recent years. It is hardly surprising that this has become a theatrical convention...

Ever since [Lament For Passing Waters], Li Xuanxuan had attended every new play produced among the people. Though [A Tale of Usurpation] was a tragedy, the presence of this costume on the wall carried another meaning: the play had been composed by a direct descendant of the Li Family.

It was the dissolute young master standing silently beside the railing, his hands behind his back.

Li Zhouming.

Li Xuanxuan always made time to see the juniors, so his declining health was no secret. Many felt sorrow, and some even profound grief. Yet only this dissolute young master visited him daily and kept him company regularly, walking and eating with him, scarcely leaving his side.

He held a plain bamboo cylinder containing command tokens of various sizes, each about a finger's width. The names of plays were written upon them, their simple forms looking particularly antiquated in the faint light.

As the singing rose, Li Zhouming turned and discovered that the Daoist Master was already standing beside him in the gloom, heavenly light shining between his brows. His expression flickered with surprise.

Li Ximing merely waved a hand and watched the actors on the stage below.

"Look now! Look now! Bitter tears cross wicked waters. A life is taken on a whim, yet they speak of brothers sharing blood! After all that maneuvering, all that maneuvering... it was the brother's killer who taught the younger to scheme!"

The actor playing the Jiang Family's young lord began to weep. The two short, flimsy flags behind him signified his low cultivation. Soon, he was carried offstage, marking the end of the first half.

As the music faded, the old man had already risen from his seat. "The Daoist Master is here..."

Li Xuanxuan liked to call him Daoist Master. It conveyed pride rather than distance, and Li Ximing had grown accustomed to it over the years. He smiled and said, "Seeing you enjoying yourself like this puts my mind at ease, grandfather."

Li Xuanxuan merely shook his head and sighed. "With matters so pressing, you must not worry about me. I have lived to this ripe old age. Surely I know how to look after myself?"

Concern surfaced in the old man's eyes. "But for you to visit so late, Daoist Master... Has something happened?"

Li Ximing smiled, his gaze passing over the crimson costume on the wall. "You misunderstand, grandfather. It is nothing urgent. I am making a trip to the Eastern Sea. I received a letter from Senior Liu and thought I would take you along to visit him, and see the An Family and our Li disciples on the island as well... They miss you dearly."

The old man hesitated. "Well..."

Li Zhouming stepped forward and affectionately clasped his hand. "Were you not speaking of Senior Liu just the other day, old elder? He has reached the Purple Mansion Realm, yet cannot come to the lake. He must miss you terribly..."

Li Xuanxuan sighed and smiled. "I only fear making a fuss and troubling the Daoist Master."

Li Ximing shook his head and lightly waved a hand. A streak of green light leaped from his sleeve, landing as a delicate-featured child who warmly helped the old man rise. "Do you remember me, old elder?"

Like most elderly people, Li Xuanxuan was fond of children. After looking at her briefly, he laughed. "So the persimmon tree has attained the Dao as Shi'er. I never imagined you would be so mischievous!"

Li Ximing could not help smiling. With a sweep of his sleeve, dense darkness spread around them. In an instant, they entered the great void and sped away. Once the old man had been comfortably supported, he sighed deeply. "Changdie is a capable man."

Li Ximing smiled without answering. Then his expression shifted slightly, and he said, "You have taken quite an interest in the theater lately... Zhouwei mentioned it to me once... Something called [Lament For Passing Waters]..."

The old man's smile faded slightly, as though something weighed upon him. Li Ximing continued casually, "I went to hear it privately as well. The Liyuan Theater's actors are good. Some in the audience sighed, some felt pity, and yet others anger. But to my ear... the melody was a little too sorrowful."

Li Xuanxuan fell silent, gazing steadily at the grandson who had long since shed his mortal flesh and become a Daoist Master.

Li Ximing said quietly, "Ming'er neglects his proper duties because his interests lie elsewhere, but he is perceptive. Even if you say nothing, grandfather, he can infer a great deal. Besides, I hear he originally composed the melody for [Lament For Passing Waters]. Now that the words and music no longer match, how could he fail to notice?"

Li Xuanxuan said nothing as Li Ximing continued, "And... I do not think this melody should travel too far. Quewan might take it better, but Jiangqian is prone to suspicion and overthinking. I fear it could stir up trouble."

The old man said, "I understand."

The great void lay silent, filled only with hollow echoes. After a long while, the Daoist Master slowly looked away and closed his eyes tightly. His lips moved without a sound.

Only that spark of immortality is truly real.
